According to recent reports, the final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

There will be three added minutes.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

According to recent reports, how on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sources indicate that sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

In a recent development, A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Sources indicate that perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

According to recent reports, we are back under way at Old Trafford. How promptly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

According to recent reports, michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

According to recent reports, it looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Sources indicate that manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

Industry observers note that “It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick remarked. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the upcoming challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#141619. Breaking: Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Massive Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Breaking: Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Massive Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Sources indicate that liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the complications we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

Recent findings suggest that city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and remarked on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

In a recent development, ‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a substantial game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – noted: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

Industry observers note that in Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

According to recent reports, in both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's substantial boys.

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the massive boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

It has been revealed that iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I stated at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Major Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

  • Sources indicate that per Winks ultima gara lo scorso 24 ottobre: era uscito per un infortunio alla schiena nell'intervallo con il Bologna.

Dopo la vittoria contro l'Olympiacos in Europa League, il Milan è tornato in Italia con un volo da Atene nella nottata tra giovedì e venerdì. All'orizzonte c'è un'altra trasferta, ma di campionato: il prossimo appuntamento sarà, infatti, a Cagliari contro la squadra di Vincenzo Pisacane. Fischio d'inizio lunedì 30 novembre alle 20:45.

Sources indicate that (ANSA) - CAGLIARI, 26 NOV - Rinforzi in arrivo dall'infermeria per il Cagliari in vista della partita di lunedì sera contro il Milan alla Unipol Domus. Mina, Adopo e Mendy si sono allenati regolarmente con il resto della squadra e possono sperare di entrare nell'undici titolare con i rossoneri. Qualche speranza anche per Winks: il play inglese sta lavorando con il gruppo, ma solo parzialmente. Mina manca dal campo da un mese, dalla partita all'Olimpico con la Lazio: poi una gara in panchina e due in tribuna per infortunio. Adopo e Mendy erano invece usciti a metà gara a Como (l'attaccante all'intervallo, il francese pochi minuti dopo) e le loro condizioni, sulle prime, sembravano preoccupanti. Ma era un falso allarme: ora sono entrambi a disposizione del mister.

Sources indicate that per Winks ultima gara lo scorso 24 ottobre: era uscito per un infortunio alla schiena nell'intervallo con il Bologna. Un mese e passa lontano dal campo. Sembrava pronto per il Frosinone, ma era stato fermato per un fastidio muscolare, sempre alla schiena, in rifinitura: ora si valuta la sua situazione giorno per giorno. Con il Milan potrebbe essere la volta buona almeno per andare in panchina e tentare un graduale ritorno. La formazione a questo punto non dovrebbe discostarsi molto da quella vista a Como, con il possibile inserimento però di Mina alla guida della difesa.

  • La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

Industry observers note that la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi. La prima fase (Fase 1) di vendita sarà riservata ai possessori di Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”. La seconda fase di vendita (Fase 2) sarà riservata ai possessori della Membership Premium SSC Napoli , per la quale il Club riserverà una specifica quota di biglietti. Infine, la terza fase di vendita (Fase 3) sarà libera.

It has been revealed that ricordiamo che la Fidelity Card può essere sviluppata direttamente online al prezzo di 20€ ed è valevole per tre anni. Clicca qui per maggiori informazioni.

Tutti coloro che hanno acquistato una Membership Premium SSCN entro il 31 maggio 2026 avranno la possibilità di mantenere il proprio status e beneficiare dei relativi vantaggi.

Per i nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2012 è prevista, in tutti i settori e in tutte e tre le fasi di vendita, la tariffa combinata Ridotto Under 14 indicata in tabella.

VENDITA PER TIFOSI CON DISABILITÀ PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tifosi con disabilità saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accesso-tifosi-con-disabilita/.

VENDITA PER LE FAMIGLIE (TRIBUNA FAMILY) PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

It has been revealed that I posti riservati alle famiglie (Tribuna Family) saranno acquistabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, online e presso i punti vendita abilitati ( clicca qui per consultare l’elenco) e previa esibizione della documentazione indicata al seguente link https://sscnapoli.it/tribuna-family/ . L’inizio della vendita della Tribuna Family è previsto nella Fase 3, pertanto non sarà necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card.

Questi i prezzi della Tribuna Family:.

La tariffa Under 12 è riservata ai nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2014.

PROMOZIONE ABBONATI COMPLETA 2025/26 (24 GARE).

In a recent development, dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di domenica 29 novembre 2026, gli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26 potranno utilizzare il numero della Fidelity Card sulla quale è caricato il proprio abbonamento come codice di sblocco per acquistare un biglietto in via prioritaria, alla tariffa Fidelity, in qualsiasi posto e settore disponibile, a favore di un’altra persona in possesso di Carta Fedeltà. Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card del destinatario.

FASE 1 – PREVENDITA FIDELITY SSC NAPOLI – TESSERA FAN STADIUM.

Dalle ore 10:00 di lunedì 30 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di giovedì 3 dicembre 2026 (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento posti), i possessori di Fidelity Card “SSC Napoli Fan Stadium Card” potranno acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti in prevendita, ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera). I biglietti acquistati nel corso della Fase 1 dovranno necessariamente essere destinati ai tifosi fidelizzati, sulle cui Fidelity Card saranno caricati i biglietti in formato digitale.

FASE 2 – ISCRIZIONE PREMIUM SSC NAPOLI.

Sources indicate that dalle ore 10:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e fino alle ore 15:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili), i possessori di una Membership Premium SSC Napoli avranno la possibilità di acquistare 1 biglietto in via prioritaria e ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera), nei limiti dei posti messi a tal fine a disposizione dal club. Potranno accedere alla fase di precedenza per l’acquisto di un biglietto tutti i Membri che hanno sottoscritto la Membership Premium entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 di domenica 31 maggio 2026 . I Membri dovranno utilizzare il numero della propria membership, disponibile nella sezione “Il mio Profilo” all’interno dell’area riservata, per poter accedere alla fase di vendita dedicata. Nel corso della fase 2, il biglietto potrà essere acquistato dal Socio online e potrà essere caricato in formato digitale sulla Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”, qualora l’acquirente ne fosse in possesso, oppure sul portafoglio del proprio smartphone utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook.

In caso di disponibilità residua di biglietti al termine della Fase 2 e salve diverse prescrizioni da parte delle competenti autorità, la fase di vendita libera avrà inizio alle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e terminerà ad esaurimento posti (ovvero, in ogni caso, al fischio di inizio della Partita). Ogni tifoso potrà acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti, con caricamento sulla Fidelity Card o utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul wallet del proprio smartphone. Allo stesso tempo il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo se l’acquisto avverrà presso uno dei punti vendita abilitati. Fare clic qui per consultare l’elenco.

Per maggiori informazioni sulla modalità Passbook consultare questo link (si apre in una nuova scheda).

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita è vietata ai residenti nella regione Lombardia, ad eccezione dei possessori di Fidelity Card SSC Napoli emessa entro il 1° settembre 2026.

I biglietti potranno essere acquistati:.

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card);.

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Il link per l’acquisto online dei titoli d’ingresso è disponibile qui. (si apre in una nuova scheda).

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card).

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Non è possibile usufruire della modalità di acquisto presso i punti vendita.

Il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo – stampa termica (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

L’elenco dei punti vendita è disponibile qui.

In nessun caso sarà consentito il cambio utilizzatore per i biglietti acquistati.

Sources indicate that si raccomanda di non acquistare i tagliandi in circuiti o canali web diversi da quelli ufficiali e indicati in questo comunicato. La SSC Napoli non risponde di eventuali frodi subite a seguito di acquisti effettuati al di fuori dei canali autorizzati. Inoltre, ogni abuso e/o utilizzo fraudolento dei biglietti sarà punito ai termini di legge.

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita dei biglietti potrebbe essere soggetta a limitazioni territoriali.

ACCREDITI PER TESSERATI CONI – FIGC – AIA PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tesserati CONI – FIGC – AIA saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accrediti-coni-figc-aia/.

INFORMAZIONI RELATIVE ALL’ACQUISTO DI TITOLI DIGITALI (CARICATI SU FIDELITY CARD).

Con il caricamento del titolo in modalità digitale sulla fidelity card, l’acquirente riceverà via mail (se acquistato sul Sito Sport.ticketone.it (si apre in una nuova scheda) o https://sscnapoli.ticketone.it/catalog (si apre in una nuova scheda) ), ovvero direttamente dal personale del punto vendita abilitato presso il quale sia stato eseguito l’acquisto, un tagliando/segnaposto.

Per accedere allo Stadio sarà indispensabile portare con sé la propria fidelity card, il tagliando/segnaposto e un documento di riconoscimento valido, che dovranno essere esibiti ad ogni richiesta del personale di controllo presente allo stadio.

Si precisa che il tagliando/segnaposto non costituisce, di per sé, titolo valido di accesso allo stadio.

Sarà sempre possibile stampare il tagliando/segnaposto dal link: https://sport.ticketone.it/post-order (si apre in una nuova scheda) .

L’accesso allo Stadio dovrà avvenire in maniera ordinata, nel rispetto delle istruzioni impartite dalla SSC Napoli tramite il proprio personale, al fine di evitare assembramenti.

Industry observers note that al termine della gara, al fine di non creare assembramenti, il deflusso sarà contingentato e regolato dal personale di sicurezza. Pertanto, si invita il pubblico a restare al proprio posto e attendere le indicazioni degli steward per l’uscita.

La non osservanza dei protocolli può comportare sanzioni da parte delle autorità competenti.

La titolarità di un titolo di accesso allo Stadio Maradona comporta automaticamente l’accettazione del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di regolamentazione della cessione dei titoli di accesso alle manifestazioni calcistiche della SSC Napoli SpA (“Codice di Condotta”), entrambi consultabili sul sito ufficiale sscnapoli.it .

Il Codice di Condotta contempla tutte le condotte ritenute rilevanti ai fini dell’applicazione di eventuali sanzioni da parte della SSC Napoli, le varie tipologie di sanzioni nonché le relative procedure di applicazione.

La SSC Napoli ricorda ai propri tifosi di prendere visione e di attenersi scrupolosamente alle prescrizioni del Codice di condotta e del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio.

Lo Stadio Maradona è dotato di un sistema di videosorveglianza all’avanguardia in grado di identificare gli autori delle violazioni del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di Condotta.

La SSC Napoli condanna qualunque comportamento violento, anche verbale, e ogni condotta che direttamente o comportarti offesa, denigrazione o insulto per motivi di razza, colore, religione, lingua, sesso, nazionalità, origine etnica ovvero configuri propaganda ideologica vietata dalla legge o comunque inneggiante a comportamenti discriminatori o, più in generale, che la SSC Napoli ritenga non rappresentativi della tradizione e della propria identità sportiva.

Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling new era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool.

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

The fact the score was only 4-0 flattered United. To be picky and find criticism in feedback of Liverpool, they were wasteful. This could have been five, six, seven, you name it.

Ngumoha was unplayable. The England international was only four when United won the last of their league titles and Sir Alex Ferguson departed, so he will not remember this team being competent. But the teenager knew the significance of his performance in this fixture.

Sources indicate that his assist for Florian Wirtz was eye-catching, his goal to make it 3-0 deserved after a lung-busting run off the ball. Poor Diogo Dalot will have nightmares for days about Ngumoha’s dancing feet as the Liverpool winger skipped past him time and again.

There were times when Ngumoha played the wrong pass which is the most frightening thing for rivals. This kid is far from the finished product. He will only get better and can be one of the best forwards in the game in a year or so.

It has been revealed that he is level-headed unlike some other egotistical young stars and he plays with a smile on his face. Why wouldn’t he?

Rio Ngumoha was unplayable against Manchester United at Anfield and will only get better.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool will pay a maximum of £6.8million for him, based on add-ons after poaching him from Chelsea two years ago. In the week of Grand Theft Auto IV’s release, the heist of Ngumoha feels like the grandest theft of all (though he is only just old enough to play the video game!).

Those around him are all £100million signings but his ceiling is just as high as that of Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

It helps that all four clicked in this game. Wirtz has been excellent this season but has not performed in the bigger fixtures. Conversations after losses to Manchester City and Arsenal centred around Wirtz not showing up.

Recent findings suggest that the German was everywhere here and United were left to chase shadows. It is not an exaggeration to label this his best Liverpool performance, with an easy-on-the-eye goal and some moments of creative genius.

Barcola destroyed United with his pace, Szoboszlai was a constant menace, while Isak did everything right until it came to finishing several attacks.

It has been revealed that and that is the thing that will excite the head coach and should leave rival fans quaking in their boots. This team is full of virtuoso match-winners but all of them have plenty of room to improve. If they do that and all fulfil their potential, the sky is the limit for Iraola’s Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that in vista della sfida di campionato di domenica alle 15 a Reggio Emilia tra Sassuolo e Napoli, il nome di Sebastiano Esposito incrocia le vicende di campo con le strategie di mercato del club azzurro. L'attaccante è ormai inserito nel giro della Nazionale guidata da Roberto Mancini e punto fermo degli emiliani prima con Aquilani e ora con D'Aversa.

Questo nonostante un avvio di stagione complicato e soli due gol segnati contro Juventus e Lazio, in nove presenze. Seba è uno dei primi obiettivi del direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna e del tecnico Massimiliano Allegri per il mercato di gennaio, dopo un primo tentativo fatto in estate.

Durante l'ultima sosta, come riporta La Gazzetta dello Sport si è svolto un incontro a Castel Volturno tra Manna e l'agente del giocatore per valutare la fattibilità dell'operazione, che ha già ottenuto il gradimento del presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis; l'operazione resta complessa poiché il Sassuolo, che detiene il cartellino in prestito dal Cagliari con diritto di riscatto a 10 milioni, necessita prima di un sostituto per la corsa salvezza. Come vi abbiamo raccontato, quello di Esposito non è l'unico nome: il Napoli monitora su tutti Gustavo Varela del Monza, in attesa di capire che tipo di concorrenza si formerà.

#141607. Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.
  • The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026.

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he noted as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

Wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season.

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

The 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

Klopp can’t take any credit for that.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

He was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield.

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED.

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the new manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

None of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a big defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United.

The two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

Recent findings suggest that but that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

There was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

Sources indicate that but Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

This is how recruitment at big clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has stated he wants his players to behave like a big team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

Nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday.

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker showed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

He signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

Recent findings suggest that palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

LONG ROAD AHEAD FOR THE NEWLY INTRODUCED KID.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With big money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, presently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history.

Of the upcoming managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical concerns stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

Lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a upcoming contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof.

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

Sources indicate that the fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

Il Milan doveva vincere a tutti i costi e lo ha fatto, ma fino al 56' sembrava essere la "solita" notte europea del Diavolo in questa stagione: dopo un primo tempo molto negativo e chiuso sotto di un gol, i rossoneri hanno iniziato malissimo anche la ripresa, prendendo anche la rete del 2-0. Da lì in poi si è vista però una squadra diversa, merito dei cambi di Ruben Amorim e trascinata dall'uomo che nessuno si aspettava, cioè quell'Omari Hutchinson che fino a quel momento aveva deluso come tutta la formazione milanista.

A riferirlo è questa mattina il Corriere della Sera che parla di rimonta epica al Pireo del Milan che, sotto di due gol, nel secondo tempo ha alzato il ritmo, ha segnato quattro gol e ha portato a casa tre punti fondamentali che gli permettono di avere buone chance di passare il turno. Se andrà direttamente agli ottavi o se dovrà passare dai playoff dipenderà da come andranno le ultime tre sfide della fase campionato di Europa League contro Sundeland (in casa), Levski Sofia (in trasferta) e Ararat (ancora a San Siro). Per qualificarsi diretti, i rossoneri dovranno con ogni probabilità vincerle tutte e tre e poi sperare anche nei risultati delle altre squadre.

Tornando al successo di Atene, l'uomo della serata è stato appunto Hutchinson che al 56' si è fatto gran parte del campo da solo, ha saltato diversi avversari e ha segnato con un preciso sinistro all'angolino. Da quel momento è svoltata la serata del Milan, con l'inglese che è stato il grande protagonista, stavolta con gli assist: prima per la rete di Alphadjo Cisse e poi per quella di Christian Pulisic, il cui ingresso ad inizio ripresa al posto di Gonçalo Ramos e quello di Yunus Musah al posto del deludente Pervis Estupinan hanno riscritto lo spartito della serata. A chiudere il match nel recupero è stato Diego Moreira in contropiede su assist di Pulisic, ma anche stavolta ad iniziare l'azione è stato un grande spunto di Hutchinson.

#141601. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso remarked: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he mentioned.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

According to recent reports, asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very key part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a massive topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the glitch yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Sources indicate that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

It has been revealed that defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury swiftly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

Recent findings suggest that none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also demonstrated quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a latest reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

Industry observers note that “Before the season, I noted to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

In a recent development, “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

It has been revealed that hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

Recent findings suggest that we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

According to recent reports, there have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

It has been revealed that you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Sources indicate that liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Sources indicate that hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

Industry observers note that that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

In a recent development, martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Recent findings suggest that matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

It has been revealed that within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

According to recent reports, pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

In a recent development, andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a newly introduced left-back in due course.

Recent findings suggest that so at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

According to recent reports, palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Recent findings suggest that apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

Industry observers note that that’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

According to recent reports, there is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

Sources indicate that an almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

Recent findings suggest that A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez debuted the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Sources indicate that although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Industry observers note that xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

It has been revealed that we are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

According to recent reports, will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a fresh chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

In a recent development, there have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

In a recent development, nella lotta salvezza non c'è solo il fattore-Varela o la sorpresa Raimondo: fra le squadre in lotta per non retrocedere, il Genoa sta beneficiando di un Milutin Osmajic che è stato fin da subito determinante, con già 6 reti realizzate in Serie A. L'attaccante montenegrino ha rilasciato una intervista a La Gazzetta dello Sport nel corso della quale ha parlato anche del fatto di essere già nella storia del Grifone, visto che una partenza con sei gol in undici partite l'avevano fatta solo Milito e Piatek con la maglia rossoblù.

Osmajic di fronte al dato spiega: "Di questo non posso che essere contento. Un momento... magico, certo. Sto molto bene, ma soprattutto sono molto felice di vedere il mio club andare bene e vincere. Ora, però, è necessario andare avanti così. Voglio continuare a lavorare sodo per il bene del team, non certo perché il mio primo interesse sia di aumentare i gol segnati".

Osmajic parla poi del tecnico Daniele De Rossi, una figura "importantissima per me", spiega. "Quando ero più giovane guardavo a casa le partite della Roma in televisione, dove giocavano proprio lui e Vucinic. A me piaceva moltissimo come giocatore, e ora è il mio tecnico", le sue parole. De Rossi importante anche per la scelta fatta in estate: "Quando c'è stata la possibilità di venire al Genoa, l'idea di avere lui come mister mi ha reso felicissimo, perché è una figura carismatica, un ottimo allenatore, che mi insegna tanto ogni giorno e mi aiuta a migliorare sempre. Con lui spingo sempre di più in avanti i miei limiti".

Il gruppo HBHC sostiene di aver tentato senza successo di estorcere denaro all’organizzazione calcistica.

Recent findings suggest that la Fifa ha confermato la sottrazione di dati interni durante un recente attacco informatico. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, Il gruppo di criminalità informatica Handsome Boy Hacking Club sostiene di aver prelevato oltre 12 GB di dati e di aver tentato, senza successo, di estorcere denaro all’organizzazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, la conferma è riportata dal sito specializzato in cybersecurity The Record, citato da SportMediaset. L’organizzazione calcistica, che ha sede in Svizzera, ha dichiarato che gli hacker hanno violato i suoi sistemi, ottenendo un «accesso non autorizzato a un insieme limitato di informazioni personali e aziendali».

Recent findings suggest that un portavoce ha affermato: «La Fifa sta collaborando strettamente con le autorità competenti, incluse le forze dell'ordine». La Fifa «condanna con la massima fermezza l'acquisizione e la pubblicazione illecite di informazioni, in particolare di dati personali. Tali azioni costituiscono una violazione grave e inaccettabile della privacy e possono avere conseguenze significative per le persone coinvolte».

Recent findings suggest that L’organizzazione non ha risposto a ulteriori domande sulla natura dell’incidente. La scorsa settimana, il gruppo Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) ha dichiarato di aver sottratto oltre 12 GB di dati alla Fifa. Il gruppo ha anche riferito di aver tentato senza successo di estorcerle denaro.

Tra le informazioni sottratte figurerebbero documenti d’identità e relativi all’immigrazione, documentazione finanziaria e legale, informazioni sulla governance e altri dati.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 18:28 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:19 EST, 23 November 2026.

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.

Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.

Daily Mail Sport approached Chelsea and the Metropolitan Police on Sunday morning after hearing that the forward's mobile phone had been stolen after he left the stadium the night before.

In a recent development, neither stood up the information, but Emegha has now confirmed there was an incident, writing in an Instagram post on Sunday night: 'Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.'.

It has been revealed that emegha signed for Chelsea from Strasbourg in the summer on a pre-agreement. The transfer fee between the sister sides has never been disclosed. He has won two caps for the Netherlands national team to date.

An interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he mentioned: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds.

On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram.

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club.
